faq.a: Yaqoob is associated with the Arabic form يَعْقُوب, whose core sense is yaqoob; jacob (prophet).

faq.q: What is the origin of Yaqoob?
faq.a: Yaqoob is associated with Arabic. Yaqoob is Arabic يَعْقُوب (Yaʿqūb), the Quranic form of the prophet Jacob.
Yes — the underlying form يَعْقُوب is Arabic.
Yaqoob can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Yaqoob should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Yaʿqūb is the Quranic Arabic form of the prophet Jacob and occurs in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Yaqoob mean in Persian?

A romanized syllable approximation is ya-qoob. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Yaqoob, yaqoob. Script forms are يَعْقُوب, یعقوب, याक़ूब.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
